report.summary: `test_book_can_be_updated` fails because the test is wrong. It updates the book with year=2001 but then asserts year=2002. The app saved and returned 2001, which is correct. Change the expected year in the test to 2001.

causes.title: Update test asserts a year different from the one it sent
causes.explanation: The test updates the book with year=2001 and then expects the fetched book to have year=2002. The update returned 200 and the stored book has year 2001, which is what was sent. The expected value in the assertion is a typo or leftover. I did not read the application's update code. The diff shows the app stored exactly what the test sent, so I see no sign of a product bug.
evidence: tests/api/test_books_api.py:23: updated = api.update_book(book["id"], title="Final title", author="Someone", year=2001)
Failure diff: {'year': 2001} != {'year': 2002}, with the other 3 fields identical
causes.suggested_fix: Change the expected year in the assertion to 2001. Better, use one variable for both the update call and the assertion so they can't drift apart.
